answer: everything that has no purpose other than helping our design and build pipeline for code belongs to code mother. now, as to why i worded it that way: we started on builds and getting builds right because doing so requires less human intervention. this has proven to be hard. while you sometimes come up with really novel questions I hadn't thought of, you also come up with questions for me about parts of the system I did not design and have to learn about to be able to offer any kind of opinion. good thing i like learning. but it's also the case that building is a cognative activity. by taking it apart we are taking apart and learning about both Claude's cognition and my own. we don't have an intention extractor yet. We did in UU, not that it was built and working or anything. but we will have eventually. one built in graph trees. it will evolve out of our current ticketing process. that's the part we're optimizing now. that's what rehersals are about. but coding is a narrow activity compared to all the things an LLM might be called on to help with. However, many of things we're learning about in the process of optimizing builds is directly applicable. so code mother owns them as helpers with her children. things that help with her children are hers. and might be models for how to do general reasoning.
